marian_page.name: Maid Marian in Disguise
marian_page.intro: Long ago, before he was an outlaw, Robin loved Marian, a lady of Locksley. Since he fled to the greenwood she has missed him every day. Now a strange page boy rides into Sherwood with a sword at his side...

nodes.text: A slim page in a blue cap blocks the forest path and draws a sword. 'Stand aside, outlaw! I seek Robin Hood, and I'll not be stopped by the likes of you.'
Robin is in a ragged disguise of his own. The page doesn't know him.

options.label: Draw your sword
options.log: 'Then come and stop me, little page!' laughs Robin, and their blades ring together.

options.label: Ask the page's name
options.log: 'My name is my own,' says the page, and swings. Robin has to draw or be beaten!

nodes.text: Robin and the page fight up and down the path for a whole hour.
nodes.win: Robin knocks the sword aside. The page cries out, and Robin knows that voice! Off comes the cap, and down tumbles a mane of auburn hair. It is Marian!
nodes.lose: The page fights so well that Robin begs for mercy. 'Robin? Is that you?' Off comes the cap, and down tumbles a mane of auburn hair. It is Marian!

nodes.text: That night there is a feast under the Major Oak. Marian will not stay in the forest: 'I can do more for you in the castle, as a lady of the court. I will be your eyes in Nottingham.' From now on, Marian may turn up on the band's jobs.

marian_word.name: Word from the Castle
marian_word.intro: A basket of bread arrives at the Major Oak, and inside the biggest loaf is a note from Marian: the Sheriff is writing a new tax on every village in the shire. The tax rolls are kept in the castle.

nodes.text: Robin and the band slip into Nottingham on market day. Marian waits by the well with an empty water jug.
'The tax rolls are in the steward's room,' whispers Marian. 'Without them, nobody can say who owes what.'

options.label: Marian fetches them
options.log: Marian strolls past the guards as cool as you please and comes back with the rolls under her cloak.

options.label: Climb in the window
options.log: Will climbs in the steward's window... and finds two guards eating his dinner.

nodes.text: 'Stop! Thieves!' The steward has missed his rolls, and the guards come running across the market.

Marian drops the tax rolls into the castle kitchen fire. 'Oh dear,' she tells the steward sweetly. 'I thought they were kindling.' The new tax is forgotten, and the Sheriff's grip on Nottingham slips.

marian_alms.name: Marian's Harvest Fair
marian_alms.intro: Marian has asked the Sheriff, very politely, to let her hold a harvest fair at Locksley 'for the poor dears.' The Sheriff agreed. He did not know who would be coming.

nodes.text: Stalls of apples and pies fill the green. Marian, in her finest gown, welcomes the villagers, and a band of strangers in green hoods.
'The people need seed corn for next year,' says Marian. 'Can the band spare some gold?'

options.label: Give 50 gold for seed corn
options.log: Every family goes home with a sack of seed corn. 'Bless Robin Hood, and bless the Lady Marian!'

options.label: Robin gives an archery show
options.log: Robin splits a willow wand at a hundred paces. The children cheer, and the fair is the happiest Locksley has seen in years.

nodes.text: Tax collectors push through the crowd. 'Half of everything here belongs to the Sheriff!'
The tax men run home without a penny. Word spreads through every village: the Lady Marian and Robin Hood stand together. All over the shire, the Sheriff's grip loosens.

marian_taken.name: Marian in the Tower
marian_taken.posted_news: Sir Guy of Gisborne has found out who has been passing the castle's secrets. Maid Marian is locked in the tower, and Guy says he will marry her!
marian_taken.intro: Sir Guy has long wanted to marry Marian, and now he has her locked in the castle's west tower. The wedding is set for tomorrow. Marian has sent no word. She cannot.

nodes.text: The band reaches the castle walls at midnight. A single candle burns at the top of the west tower.
How will the band get in?

options.label: Dress as wedding monks
options.log: Tuck leads a line of very large 'monks' across the drawbridge, singing very badly. The guards let them in.

options.label: Climb the ivy
options.log: Halfway up the ivy, the band is spotted from the walls!

nodes.text: Guards on the tower stair!
At the top of the stair, Sir Guy himself blocks the door, sword drawn. 'She's mine, Hood!'
Marian is free! She grabs the bell rope, rings the castle bell to wake the whole town, and slides down it into the courtyard. 'Took you long enough,' she says, and kisses Robin.
Out through the gate before the garrison is awake!

marian_wedding.name: Robin and Marian Wed
marian_wedding.intro: Some say Robin and Marian were married in the little church at Edwinstowe, others under the Major Oak itself. Friar Tuck says it was both, and he should know, because he did it.

nodes.text: The whole greenwood is hung with ribbons. Friar Tuck has polished his bald head until it shines.
Who will walk Marian to the oak?

options.label: Little John
options.log: Little John walks Marian down the forest aisle, sniffing loudly the whole way.

options.label: Alan-a-Dale, singing
options.log: Alan-a-Dale leads her in with a song so lovely that even the birds stop to listen.

nodes.text: 'I forbid it!' The Bishop of Hereford has come to spoil the wedding, with Sir Guy's men behind him.

The Bishop runs off without his hat, and Friar Tuck marries Robin Hood and Maid Marian under the Major Oak. Marian leaves the castle for good and makes her home at Major Oak Camp. She still rides out on the band's jobs, and with the forest so close, she is a little more help than before.

will_meets_robin.name: The Stranger in Scarlet
will_meets_robin.intro: Folk near Locksley speak of a young dandy in fine scarlet who strolls the glades as if he owned them. Robin goes to see for himself.

nodes.text: Robin, newly outlawed, sees a young man in fine scarlet strolling through the glade, sniffing a rose.
'Stand!' says Robin. The stranger yawns. 'Must I?'

options.label: Ask for a toll
options.log: 'A toll? From me?' The stranger draws his sword with a flourish.

options.label: Challenge him to a bout
options.log: 'A bout? Delightful.' The stranger draws his sword with a flourish.

nodes.text: Bow against blade in the glade!
nodes.win: Robin trips the stranger into a gorse bush. 'Ow! All right, all right!'
nodes.lose: The stranger flicks Robin's hood over his eyes. 'Shall we call it a draw?'

nodes.text: 'Will Gamwell is my name, Robin. I'm your own cousin, come to find you. May I join your band?' Ever after, the outlaws call him Will Scarlet.

little_john_bridge.name: The Stranger on the Bridge
little_john_bridge.intro: Robin goes walking alone in the greenwood, looking for adventure. Will says he'll keep the fire warm.

nodes.text: Robin follows the brook to a narrow log bridge, just wide enough for one.
A giant of a man steps onto the far end. 'Back you go, little fellow. I was here first!'

options.label: Cut a staff and settle it
options.log: Robin cuts a stout oak staff. The giant grins and twirls his own.

options.label: Bow and let him pass
options.log: 'Polite!' booms the giant. 'But I'll still have a bout with you, for the fun of it.'

nodes.text: Quarterstaves on the bridge! Whoever lands in the brook loses.
nodes.win: Robin's staff sweeps the giant off the log. SPLASH! He comes up roaring with laughter.
nodes.lose: SPLASH! Robin lands in the brook. The giant hauls him out by the collar, laughing.

nodes.text: 'John Little's my name,' says the giant, wringing out his hood. 'You fight fair. Will you have me in your band?' The outlaws name him Little John.

tuck_ford.name: The Friar of Fountain Dale
tuck_ford.intro: Villagers tell of a jolly friar at Fountain Dale who can swing a staff better than any soldier.

nodes.text: Robin and Little John find a stout friar fishing at the ford, humming a hymn.
The river is cold and deep. The friar is big and dry.

options.label: Ask him to carry Robin across
options.log: The friar carries Robin across... then halfway back, tips him into the river! 'Your turn to carry me, friend!'

options.label: Offer to carry him across
options.log: Robin carries the friar across, puffing. On the far bank the friar chuckles and pushes him in. 'For the exercise!'

nodes.text: Wet and laughing, Robin draws his sword. The friar whistles, and his hounds come bounding!
nodes.win: The hounds roll over for a belly rub, and the friar sits down puffing. 'Enough! Enough!'
nodes.lose: The friar plants his staff on Robin's chest. 'Do you yield, wet one?' Everyone falls about laughing.

nodes.text: 'Friar Tuck,' says he, shaking Robin's hand. 'An outlaw band needs someone to say grace and patch up bruises. I'll come.'

alan_wedding.name: The Wedding at Edwinstowe
alan_wedding.intro: A minstrel sits weeping by the road. His sweetheart Ellen is to be married today, against her will, to a rich old knight.

nodes.text: 'I am Alan-a-Dale,' says the minstrel. 'Ellen loves me, but her father wants the knight's gold.' Robin has a plan.
The Bishop of Hereford leads the procession to the church.

options.label: Robin goes in dressed as a harper
options.log: Robin strolls in with a harp. 'A song for the bride? First, a question: does she want this wedding?' Ellen shakes her head.

options.label: Blow the horn at once
options.log: Robin's horn rings out and the Merry Men pour from the trees!

nodes.text: 'Seize those outlaws!' cries the Bishop. His guards step forward.
Friar Tuck marries Alan and Ellen on the spot. The whole village cheers, and Alan picks up his lute: 'My songs are yours, Robin.'
The happy couple ride for Sherwood with the band.

silver_arrow.name: The Silver Arrow
silver_arrow.intro: The Sheriff announces an archery contest. The prize is an arrow of pure silver. Everyone knows it's a trap to catch Robin, and Robin goes anyway.

nodes.text: Robin pulls a patched brown hood low and joins the crowd of archers. The rest of the band hides among the townsfolk.
The target is set at a hundred paces. The Sheriff's own champion steps up to shoot against the hooded stranger.
nodes.win: Robin's last arrow splits the champion's arrow clean in two! The crowd roars.
nodes.lose: The champion wins by a hair, but the crowd roars for the hooded stranger, and the Sheriff looks hard at him.

nodes.text: The Sheriff hands over the silver arrow, peers under the hood, and shouts: 'It's him! Seize Robin Hood!'
Over the town wall and away! Riders give chase.

wanted_posters.name: Wanted: Robin Hood
wanted_posters.intro: The Sheriff hits back. Wanted posters are going up in every village, and the villagers are made to pay a 'bounty tax' to fund the reward.

nodes.text: Posters are nailed to every tree in Edwinstowe: WANTED, ROBIN HOOD. The picture looks more like a turnip in a hat.
The Sheriff's crier reads the poster aloud while soldiers go door to door for the bounty tax.

options.label: Tear the posters down
options.log: Robin rips down the nearest poster. 'That's not even my good side!'

options.label: Improve the picture
options.log: Will draws a much handsomer Robin on every poster, and gives the Sheriff's face a pig's snout. The villagers howl with laughter.

nodes.text: The crier squeals for the guards! The tax men clutch their money bags.
The band hands the bounty tax back to the villagers. An old woman tucks a poster into Robin's quiver. 'For luck, lad. They'll send hunters after you next.'

hunters_hunted.name: The Hunters Hunted
hunters_hunted.place: Black Hob's camp at the crossing
hunters_hunted.intro: Black Hob, captain of the bounty hunters, has camped at the crossroads with his hounds. He boasts he'll have Robin Hood in a sack by Sunday.

nodes.text: The band creeps through the gorse toward the smoke of Hob's campfire.
Hob's men are dicing by the fire. A hound lifts its nose and sniffs the wind.

options.label: Walk in bold as brass
options.log: 'Looking for me?' says Robin, strolling into the firelight.

nodes.text: Black Hob leaps up with a net in each hand. 'Two hundred gold, and it's mine!'
Tied up in his own net, Hob grumbles out a secret: an old sally port under the castle's west wall, where the moat runs dry. 'The Sheriff never paid me anyway.'

storm_castle.name: Storming Nottingham Castle
storm_castle.intro: The Sheriff has filled his dungeon with villagers who could not pay the bounty tax. Thanks to Black Hob's secret, the band knows a way in. Tonight they storm Nottingham Castle!

nodes.text: At dusk the band wades the dry moat and squeezes through the old sally port under the west wall.
A narrow stair, and two sleepy guards at the top.

options.label: Tuck brings them cider
options.log: Friar Tuck offers the guards a flask of his best cider. Soon they are snoring like pigs.

nodes.text: Into the courtyard! Torches flare and the alarm bell clangs.
The dungeon door, and beyond it the Sheriff's treasury. There's only time for one before the garrison comes.

options.label: Free the prisoners
options.log: Little John bends the dungeon bars apart. Out pour farmers, millers and widows, cheering the band.

options.label: Open the treasury
options.log: Will picks the lock. Chests of tax money! On the way past, Little John tosses the jailer's keys through the dungeon bars.

nodes.text: On the battlements stand the Sheriff and Sir Guy. 'Seize them! Seize them all!'
Sir Guy topples off the battlements into a hay cart, and the Sheriff flees out of the back gate in his nightshirt. The people of Nottingham pour into the streets, cheering. Sherwood is free!
